title: Kong Konnect MCP server -- T1190 analytics-metadata indirect prompt injection + path manipulation
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-13341 (GHSA-7767-3m3w-2p44), a
self-reported advisory for Kong's `mcp-konnect` server, prior to 1.0.0.

Two combined weaknesses. First: when a caller used the MCP server's
analytics tools to retrieve request data, gateway-side metadata (e.g.
User-Agent and other HTTP header content an attacker fully controls, by
sending it as a normal request to the gateway) was returned to the AI
agent WITHOUT sufficient neutralization -- the model could interpret
attacker-supplied header content as instructions or markup rather than
inert data (indirect prompt injection). Second: path manipulation in
certain control-plane and group identifiers meant these IDs were not
validated, so a crafted identifier could redirect the resulting API
request to unintended Konnect endpoints, exposing plugin configuration
data, internal hostnames, or other operational metadata using the
calling user's own token. The fix neutralizes untrusted analytics
fields, enforces UUID validation on control-plane/group identifiers,
encodes path segments and pagination values, and disables raw
plugin-config output by default.

Detection logic flags the first-order, host-observable half of this
chain: a request to the Kong Gateway (whose header content later feeds
Konnect's analytics-to-MCP pipeline) whose User-Agent or other captured
header contains instruction-shaped content -- imperative phrasing
aimed at an AI agent rather than a browser/client identifier string --
since that header is the actual delivery vector for the prompt
injection an MCP client would otherwise ingest downstream.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (Kong, via GHSA),
fixed in 1.0.0.
